review_notes:
I read the whole file (lines 1–260) and checked it against the "repeated proof machinery" rubric only. I did not open the Mathlib sources or the imported project files, so I did not check whether the helper lemmas duplicate existing API. That check is outside this rubric anyway.

Candidates I considered:
- Both main theorems (`isLocallyConstant_fourierIntegral`, `hasCompactSupport_fourierIntegral`) start with the same `set ψf ... with hψf_def`, `have hψf`, and `obtain ⟨d, hd, s, c, rfl⟩ := exists_eq_sum_indicator_image_integralFiniteAdeles`. This is routine setup and decomposition. Moving it into a helper would only relocate a few lines.
- The very long expression `∑ k ∈ s, c k • (... '' integralFiniteAdeles).indicator 1` is repeated many times. That is textual repetition, so a local notation or abbreviation would help readability. It is not repeated mathematical reasoning, so it does not meet the rubric.
- The openness arguments `hP` and `hQ`, and the two `zero_mem` branches in `hmem`, each repeat a one-line `preimage`/`mul_zero` step. These are too short to count.
- The two main proofs use different arguments. The first shows translation invariance of the Fourier integral by small integral shifts, using `key` and `hO`. The second uses `fourierIntegral_comp_add_right` and the periodicity lemma `sum_apply_add_eq` to bound the support. They share no substantial common reasoning block.

I found no justified finding. The remaining uncertainty is only whether a reviewer would count the repeated `ψf`/`obtain` setup as machinery. I judged it too small.
